messages.subject: Re: [poppr] error in loading data
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

There are a couple of issues here that the error message is trying to help with:

1. You need to set the ploidy flag in read.genalex() to the maximum ploidy. You mention that you have some diploid and some triploid individuals, but you've coded your data as tetraploid (4 columns per locus):

mydata <- read.genalex("mydata.csv", ploidy = 4)

(If you decide to remove those extra zero columns, you should then set ploidy = 3)

2. Cell C1 contains the number 2. Unless you specify the exact population sizes in the next two cells, you should set cell C1 to 1 (this is documented in https://grunwaldlab.github.io/Population_Genetics_in_R/Data_Preparation.html#basic-format)

Hope that helps,

Zhian

messages.subject: Re: [poppr] How to get p.Ia value
messages.body_plain:
All of these methods use randomizations to obtain the p-value. These randomizations must shuffle the data and recompute the index, and thus can be time intensive, especially if you have a large data set. I'm afraid that's the only way a p-value for the index of association is calculated.

pair.ia will run especially slow because it calculates the index and a p-value for each locus separately.

messages.subject: Re: [poppr] How to get p.Ia value
messages.body_plain:
Hi Ying,

Yes, if you set sample = 99, then it will randomize the data and recalculate the index 99 times. With any randomization procedure, more samples will give you a more precise p-value (but that also depends on your sample size).

Using set.seed(1000) means that your sampling will be reproducible.

Best,

Zhian

messages.subject: Re: [poppr] bruvo.boot
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

1) The way you are defining the repeats is not exactly correct. You want the length of the motif (CT), not the length of the sequence (15). Bruvo's model assumes that you do not have mixed motifs, so any model you choose will be wrong. For the repeats you've shown, you may want to take the average of distances at 2 and 4 nucleotides or just set it at 3 nucleotides.

2) No. But you can use the hierfstat package. That has options for calculating inbreeding and will take the genind object as input.

Best,

Zhian

messages.subject: Re: [poppr] AMOVA and provesti.dist
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

1) You interpret the p-value the same as any other simulation-based p-value. It's the fraction of the simulated data sets that had a value more extreme or equal to the observed value. The default output uses the ade4 package, which is notoriously unhelpful in its output for AMOVA (example: "samples" in this case really means "populations"). using the method = "pegas" flag might help you a bit more.

2) The warning of negative branches is not uncommon for clonal systems, which can have negative branches in neighbor-joining trees. The warning is informing you that there were negative branches and that they were corrected according to the Kuhner and Felsenstein (1994) method where the negative branch is set to zero by borrowing length from its sibling (which often results in the sibling going to zero).
